vulnerabilities.type: Unprotected/rewritable initialization (BuilderWallet takeover) leading to theft of fees
vulnerabilities.explanation: BuilderWallet is intended to be a deterministic fee-recipient wallet deployed by BuilderFactory, with the ability for a designated `builderAdmin` to sweep accumulated ERC20 fees. However, `init(address _builderAdmin)` has no access control and no one-time initialization guard. Any address can call `init` at any time (including after the factory initializes it) to set/overwrite `builderAdmin`. Once overwritten, the attacker can call `sweep()` and steal all tokens held by the wallet. This is a concrete loss-of-funds vector for all fees routed to builder wallets (computed by RiskEngine via CREATE2). No trusted role compromise is required; only knowledge of the wallet address is needed (deterministic from builderCode).
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario:
1) Attacker computes or observes a builder wallet address (deterministic via builderCode / on-chain events).
2) Attacker calls `BuilderWallet(wallet).init(attackerEOA)` to set themselves as `builderAdmin` (or re-set it after legitimate initialization).
3) When the protocol sends builder fees to `wallet`, attacker calls `BuilderWallet(wallet).sweep(token, attackerEOA)` to transfer the entire token balance out.
4) Legitimate builder can no longer sweep (attacker can keep re-initializing to themselves).
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix:
Restrict and one-time guard initialization. For example:
- `function init(address _builderAdmin) external { require(msg.sender == FACTORY, "NOT_FACTORY"); require(builderAdmin == address(0), "ALREADY_INIT"); require(_builderAdmin != address(0), "ZERO_ADMIN"); builderAdmin = _builderAdmin; }`
Alternatively, set `builderAdmin` in the constructor (as an immutable) and remove `init()` entirely, incorporating `builderAdmin` into the CREATE2 init code.

prediction.overall_explanation: Most of RiskEngine is view/pure math and guardian-gated administrative calls, with no obvious direct fund-handling except guardian `collect`. The major exploitable issue is in the auxiliary BuilderWallet: its `init()` is publicly callable and can be called repeatedly, allowing any attacker to seize `builderAdmin` and steal any ERC20s sent to builder fee-recipient wallets. This directly threatens protocol fee flows routed via builder codes.
